conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Trim QQQI to 15% to slightly reduce income exposure.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a hedge. Expect moderate growth with controlled drawdowns.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name mandate.
Add to SOXL, targeting 6%, and SPAL, targeting 6%, to increase leveraged ETF exposure.
Add to CRWD, targeting 20%, to lean into a strong uptrend.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-scoring setups. Be aware this strategy significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk, and leveraged ETFs experience daily decay.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to prioritize income for yield.
Trim QQQ to 10% to reduce broad index exposure.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income by rotating into income ETFs and cutting high-beta names. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
